points.description: States that a pointer is an address of a location in memory (a variable that holds a memory address). Any wording is fine, e.g. 'stores the address of another variable'.
points.partial_credit: Half or more if vague or slightly wrong, e.g. says it 'refers to' or 'points to' a variable or memory without clearly saying address.

points.description: Makes clear that the address is of a memory location (e.g. a variable or place in memory), not just a value or data.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying a pointer is (or holds) the address of a memory location, in any wording, even briefly. Give part marks for vague answers such as 'it points to something' or 'refers to a variable' without saying address. Give no marks for answers that only discuss related things (arrays, syntax, references) without stating the address idea; extra correct detail is fine.
